terra.problem: The passage does not say the barley field was still standing afterward.
The passage does not say the Philistine camp was parked in front of the well.
The whole water story does not happen in Bethlehem. David is at a stronghold when he receives and pours out the water.
The passage does not say the Philistine garrison was why the well mattered to David.
The passage says David refused to drink the water and poured it out. It does not establish that nobody else drank or received any of it.
The passage does not say whether facing the two champions was a rough day for Benaiah.
Edom's proximity to Moab is a fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The line about a name being pulled to the "wrong spot" uses "wrong" about a possible answer mix-up.
The passage calls Benaiah a man of valor but does not say the lion exploit is why it calls him that.
The passage does not establish that Benaiah never covered anything or walked away.
The passage does not say whether Benaiah waited before going into the pit.
The workplace punchline makes light of the Egyptian being killed.
The passage does not establish that nobody came to help. Saying the fight was just Benaiah and a club also leaves out the Egyptian and the spear Benaiah used.
The passage does not say David trusted Benaiah or appointed him because of his exploits.
Grapes are not a food in the passage or an answer on this card, so "grape duty" breaks the food rule.
The passage does not say the lion and Egyptian exploits happened before Benaiah's appointment.
The passage does not say Benaiah personally kept watch over the king or that the two exploits happened before his appointment.
